item.title: Night Trains Return Not Out of Nostalgia, But Because Short-Haul Slots Are Full
item.description:
Discussions about overnight sleeper trains almost always drift into romantic postcards of brass lamps and dining cars. Yet transport planners backing new rolling-stock orders in Vienna, Zurich, and Stockholm rarely mention nostalgia.

They look at congested daytime high-speed corridors and capped regional airport slots. Between midnight and five in the morning, thousands of kilometers of electrified mainline track sit largely unused by passenger traffic.

Economics of Rolling Stock Availability

For decades, night trains struggled because bespoke sleeper coaches were expensive to maintain in small batches. Standardized modular sleeping cars ordered jointly by neighboring state railways finally bend unit maintenance curves downward.
